# ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io Weekly Report (Jun 21 - 27, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week’s activity focused on hardening protocol security and refining infrastructure designs to support the evolving Superchain ecosystem. Key achievements include the finalization of the PCD Infrastructure design and significant progress in test coverage for edge-case settlement scenarios. While the team addressed critical "intrinsic gas" errors affecting the Optimism Sepolia network following the Karst hard fork, development also shifted toward optimizing the `op-reth` and `kona-node` codebases to reduce technical debt and improve database interoperability.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
While no major technical features were merged into the main repository this week, significant groundwork was laid for ecosystem expansion and infrastructure efficiency.

### Ecosystem Expansion
- **Token Integrations:** A new pull request was initiated to integrate the OUTFLOW token ([#1332](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1332)). This represents an expansion of the Base ecosystem into real-world assets, specifically focusing on solar energy ERC-20 tokens from Outflow Labs.

### Infrastructure & Tooling Optimization
- **Reth Integration:** Efforts are underway to streamline `op-reth` by reusing upstream slot-preimage seeding helpers ([#21523](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/21523)). This move aims to eliminate code duplication and align more closely with the next Reth release.
- **Kona-node SafeDB:** Development progressed on the `SafeDB` implementation for `kona-node` ([#20278](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/20278)). The team is currently implementing a `SafeDBv1` trait as a direct port of existing designs while simultaneously architecting `SafeDBv2` to improve interface flexibility and proof compatibility.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage
The week saw a balance between resolving complex protocol testing issues and triaging regressions from recent hard forks.

### Closed Issues
- **Protocol Security & Testing:** The team successfully closed a major effort in SDM test hardening ([#21324](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/21324)). This improved the protocol's resilience by adding coverage for ETH supply conservation, post-execution settlement underflows, and out-of-order index payload scenarios.
- **Design Approvals:** The design documentation for PCD (Proof Carrying Data) Infrastructure support was finalized and closed ([#21327](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/21327)), clearing the way for future implementation.

### New & Active Issues
- **Optimism Sepolia Gas Regression:** A high-priority issue ([#21457](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/21457)) remains active regarding "intrinsic gas too high" errors on OP Sepolia. The bug, triggered by the Karst hard fork, affects `eth_estimateGas` across multiple RPC providers. While users can bypass this by setting an explicit `gasLimit`, a formal fix is slated for the upcoming release.
- **Technical Debt:** New tracking was added for `op-reth` to remove redundant seeding helpers in favor of upstream solutions, ensuring better maintainability ([#21523](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/21523)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by deep technical discussions regarding database architecture and protocol standards. The dialogue surrounding the `SafeDB` implementation ([#20278](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/20278)) highlights a concerted effort to balance rapid implementation (v1) with long-term architectural integrity (v2). Additionally, the community remained highly engaged in troubleshooting the OP Sepolia gas issues, providing the necessary data points for maintainers to confirm the scope of the Karst hard fork regression.
